draft.title: Depth cues
card: Depth perception is judging how far away objects are, even though the image on each retina is flat. The brain uses depth cues to do this.

cues that need both eyes. Retinal disparity is the small difference between the images in each eye: the closer an object is, the bigger the difference. Convergence is the inward turn of the eyes to focus on a near object: the closer the object, the more they turn inward.
cues that work with one eye. Linear perspective is the way parallel lines, such as rail tracks, seem to meet in the distance. Interposition is when an object that blocks part of another seems closer.
A person with sight in one eye can still use monocular cues, so they can still judge depth, though less precisely.
draft.remember: Binocular cues need two eyes. Monocular cues work with one.

a.q: Which depth cue relies on the brain comparing the slightly different images from the left and right eyes?
a.why: Retinal disparity is the difference between the two retinal images, so it needs both eyes. Convergence is also binocular, but it is the inward turn of the eyes, not a comparison of images.
a.clue: Think of the cue that is about two images, not eye movement.

b.q: Priya covers one eye and looks at a road. She can still tell that a parked car partly hiding a bin is in front of the bin. Which cue does she use?
b.why: The car blocks part of the bin, so this is interposition. It works with one eye, so it is monocular. Retinal disparity is binocular, so it could not be used with one eye covered.
b.clue: Which cue is about one object blocking another, and does it need two eyes?

check.summary: No problems found. The facts about binocular and monocular cues are correct, both questions have exactly one right answer, and the explanations match the card.
